arxiv-1511-09069.title: Serendipitous Science from the K2 Mission Journal: Astronomy in Focus, Volume 1
arxiv-1511-09069.creator: Derek L. Buzasi 1, Lindsey Carboneau 1, Carly Hessler 1, Andy Lezcano 1, Heather Preston 1,2
arxiv-1511-09069.description: Abstract The K2 mission is a repurposed use of the Kepler spacecraft to perform high-precision photometry of selected fields in the ecliptic. We have developed an aperture photometry pipeline for K2 data which performs dynamic automated aperture mask selection, background estimation and subtraction, and positional decorrelation to minimize the effects of spacecraft pointing jitter.

arxiv-1906-00826.description: Abstract The phase state of dense matter in the intermediate density range ( ∼ \sim 1-10 times the nuclear saturation density) is both intriguing and unclear and could have important observable effects in the present gravitational wave era of neutron stars.

arxiv-2105-09834.title: Limit Multiplicity For Unitary Groups and The Stable Trace Formula
arxiv-2105-09834.creator: Mathilde Gerbelli-Gauthier
arxiv-2105-09834.description: Abstract . We give upper bounds on limit multiplicities of certain non-tempered representations of unitary groups U ⁡ ( a , b ) U(a,b) , conditionally on the endoscopic classification of representations. Our result applies to some cohomological representations, and we give applications to the growth of cohomology of cocompact arithmetic subgroups of unitary groups.

arxiv-2212-11797.title: Global Kuranishi charts and a product formula in symplectic Gromov–Witten theory
arxiv-2212-11797.creator: Amanda Hirschi, Mohan Swaminathan
arxiv-2212-11797.description: Abstract . We construct global Kuranishi charts for the moduli spaces of stable pseudoholomorphic maps to a closed symplectic manifold in all genera. This is used to prove a product formula for symplectic Gromov–Witten invariants. As a consequence we obtain a Künneth formula for quantum cohomology. 1. Introduction 1.1. Background Let (X,\omega) be a closed symplectic manifold.

arxiv-2307-16500.title: Deciding Linear Height and Linear Size-to-Height Increase of Macro Tree Transducers
arxiv-2307-16500.creator: Paul Gallot, Sebastian Maneth, Keisuke Nakano, Charles Peyrat
arxiv-2307-16500.description: Abstract We present a novel normal form for (total deterministic) macro tree transducers (mtts), called “depth proper normal form”. If an mtt is in this normal form, then it is guaranteed that each parameter of each state appears at arbitrary depths in the output trees of that state.

arxiv-2310-18498.title: GPT-4 Vision on Medical Image Classification – A Case Study on COVID-19 Dataset
arxiv-2310-18498.creator: Ruibo Chen, Tianyi Xiong, Yihan Wu, Guodong Liu, Zhengmian Hu, Lichang Chen, Yanshuo Chen, Chenxi Liu, Heng Huang
arxiv-2310-18498.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ruibo Chen, Tianyi Xiong, Yihan Wu, Guodong Liu, Zhengmian Hu, Lichang Chen, Yanshuo Chen, Chenxi Liu, Heng Huang. 1
Introduction

In the intricate landscape of modern healthcare, medical image classification emerges as a pivotal task, driving crucial decisions in diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient management. This process involves the systematic categorization of various types of medical imagery—including X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and ultrasound—into distinct classes that assist healthcare professionals in identifying anomalies, understanding physiological phenomena, and detecting diseases at early stages.

arxiv-2409-07284.title: TLD-READY: Traffic Light Detection - Relevance Estimation and Deployment Analysis
arxiv-2409-07284.creator: Nikolai Polley, Svetlana Pavlitska, Yacin Boualili, Patrick Rohrbeck, Paul Stiller, Ashok Kumar Bangaru, J. Marius Zöllner
arxiv-2409-07284.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nikolai Polley, Svetlana Pavlitska, Yacin Boualili, Patrick Rohrbeck, Paul Stiller, Ashok Kumar Bangaru, J. Marius Zöllner. Effective traffic light detection is a critical component of the perception stack in autonomous vehicles. This work introduces a novel deep-learning detection system while addressing the challenges of previous work. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset amalgamation, including the Bosch Small Traffic Lights Dataset, LISA, the DriveU Traffic Light Dataset, and a proprietary dataset from Karlsruhe, we ensure a robust evaluation across varied scenarios.

pmc-10722498.title: Fixing Flavins: Hijacking a Flavin Transferase for Equipping Flavoproteins with a Covalent Flavin Cofactor
pmc-10722498.creator: Yapei Tong, Saniye G. Kaya, Sara Russo, Henriette J. Rozeboom, Hein J. Wijma, Marco W. Fraaije
pmc-10722498.description: Most flavin-dependent enzymes contain a dissociable flavin cofactor. We present a new approach for installing in vivo a covalent bond between a flavin cofactor and its host protein. By using a flavin transferase and carving a flavinylation motif in target proteins, we demonstrate that “dissociable” flavoproteins can be turned into covalent flavoproteins.

pmc-11289262.title: Predicting hormone receptor status in invasive breast cancer through radiomics analysis of long-axis and short-axis ultrasound planes
pmc-11289262.creator: Jiangfeng Wu, Lifang Ge, Yinghong Guo, Anli Zhao, Jincao Yao, Zhengping Wang, Dong Xu
pmc-11289262.description: The hormone receptor (HR) status plays a significant role in breast cancer, serving as the primary guide for treatment decisions and closely correlating with prognosis. This study aims to investigate the predictive value of radiomics analysis in long-axis and short-axis ultrasound planes for distinguishing between HR-positive and HR-negative breast cancers.

pmc-11478659.title: The Effects of Mechanical Loading on Resonant Response of a Conformal Load-Bearing Antenna System
pmc-11478659.creator: Shouxun Lu, Kelvin J. Nicholson, Joel Patniotis, John Wang, Wing Kong Chiu
pmc-11478659.description: Glass fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) is a suitable substrate material for constructing a Conformal Load-Bearing Antenna Structure (CLAS). The relative permittivity of the CLAS substrate, which determines its resonant frequency, is affected by damage sustained by GFRP. This paper investigates the effects of damage (induced by mechanically loading the substrate) on the resonant response of the CLAS.

pmc-11605121.title: Effects of foot–ground friction and age-related gait changes on falls during walking: a computational study using a neuromusculoskeletal model
pmc-11605121.creator: Naoto Izumi, Takashi Yoshida, Toshiaki Nishi, Kei Masani, Takeshi Yamaguchi
pmc-11605121.description: We used a neuromusculoskeletal model of bipedal walking to examine the effects of foot–ground friction conditions and gait patterns on slip- and trip-induced falls. We developed three two-dimensional neuro-musculoskeletal models in a self-organized manner representing young adults, elderly non-fallers, and elderly fallers. We simulated walking under different foot-ground friction conditions.

pmc-12649706.title: Development and Validation of the Future Career Insecurity Scale (FCIS) in Law Students
pmc-12649706.creator: Cuiyu Lan, Xinying Weng, Qi-Lu Huang, Liqian Yu, Ruizhe Wang, Jie Su, Tianshu Zhou, Tingjian Lou, Yinlin Li, Wei Li, Maite Barrios
pmc-12649706.description: The transition from university to the workforce is a major developmental milestone that can generate significant psychological distress, especially for students in high-stakes professional programs such as law. Traditional measures of career-related anxiety often overlook the multidimensional nature of career insecurity and its culturally specific expressions.

pmc-13029923.title: From Biomarkers to Biosensors: Transforming Comorbidity Management in Dialysis Care
pmc-13029923.creator: Ali Fardoost, Koosha Karimi, Aratrika Bhattacharya, Viresh Patel, Matthew Lucien Saintyl, Samanthia Grace Welsh, Mehdi Javanmard
pmc-13029923.description: Patients receiving dialysis treatments suffer from a high rate of systemic comorbid conditions, including cardiovascular disease, mineral and bone disorders, chronic inflammation, amyloidosis, and recurring infections, leading to increased morbidity and mortality rates despite the progress made in the field of renal replacement therapies.

uslaw-usc-t36-s30902.title: 36 U.S.C. § 30902 — Purposes
uslaw-usc-t36-s30902.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s30902.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 309 (Boy Scouts Of America). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The purposes of the corporation are to promote, through organization, and cooperation with other agencies, the ability of boys to do things for themselves and others, to train them in scoutcraft, and to teach them patriotism.
